title: Adoption, Enablement And Sustainable Handover Checkpoint

questions.prompt: 30 of 100 eligible agents are active, and 60 were trained. What is adoption among eligible agents?

options.label: 50%, because untrained eligible users should disappear from every denominator.
100%, because every active agent opened the application.
30%, with 50% separately describing active users among trained agents.

questions.explanation: Denominators answer different questions. Eligible adoption is 30/100; trained-user activation is 30/60. Neither can silently substitute for the other.

questions.prompt: A bot marks a ticket resolved but it reopens next day. Under a no-reopen-for-seven-days rule, how is it counted?

options.label: Removed from all metrics because the result is inconvenient.
Not resolved for that outcome metric; record the repeat work.
Resolved because the first automated status was positive.

questions.explanation: The declared observation window determines success. Premature counting and selective exclusion hide rework.

questions.prompt: Which handover test provides useful evidence of customer capability?

options.label: A maintainer deploys and recovers a fixture using the runbook without the builder driving.
A slide deck was emailed to an unconfirmed recipient.
The builder says the deployment is straightforward.

questions.explanation: Independent teach-back tests instructions and ownership. Sending documents and confidence do not show that another person can operate the system.

questions.prompt: High usage and low answer accuracy are observed together. What should the review conclude?

options.label: Usage proves correctness, so ignore the incorrect answers.
Accuracy cannot matter if the customer paid for the pilot.
Adoption and quality differ; investigate quality despite high usage.

questions.explanation: Usage, quality and commercial activity are distinct. A valuable review preserves both positive and negative evidence.
